title: Emotional skills and health assessment in interventions for intimate partner violence perpetrators: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
interventionFamily: Perpetrator programmes incorporating emotional skills, usually within CBT; emotion regulation, anger management, communication and empathy.

relevance.population: Adult men and women who perpetrate IPV in community, military and online intervention samples
relevance.exposureEvidence: Eligibility and study population descriptions explicitly concern IPV perpetrators, IPV-exposed survivors/children, or IPV prevention.
relevance.rationale: Adds a methods-supported map of emotional-skills interventions while retaining weak official-record evidence and preventing positive-outcome vote counting from becoming an efficacy claim.
relevance.transferLimit: No review registration or published protocol. Heterogeneous interventions and active controls often shared emotional components; four pilot/feasibility trials and frequent self-report limit causal attribution to emotional skills alone.

age.reportedRange: Reported study mean ages range from 27 to 60.5 years; individual age range not established.

country: United States (9 trials), Spain (2), Netherlands, United Kingdom, Norway and Sweden (1 each).
setting: Mainly community programmes; one military trial and one online trial.

sampleSize.description: 15 primary trial reports with 2,390 reported participants; 1,369 intervention and 1,021 comparator. Pooled trial participants are not new independent studies.

intervention.description: Perpetrator programmes incorporating emotional skills, usually within CBT; emotion regulation, anger management, communication and empathy.
intervention.dose: Single-session to more than 16-session programmes; duration and emotional-content intensity varied.
intervention.provider: Health professionals, psychologists, therapists and psychology students; relevant IPV experience reported in four trials.

comparator: Mostly heterogeneous active interventions; some no-treatment, usual-care or placebo comparisons.

outcomes.name: Official IPV recidivism
outcomes.result: Only one of five trials favored intervention
outcomes.uncertainty: Narrative synthesis; no pooled recidivism effect.
outcomes.primaryStatus: Review outcome; no participant-randomized trial conducted by this publication.

outcomes.name: Any selected recidivism or associated outcome
outcomes.result: Eight of 15 trials reported a favorable difference
outcomes.uncertainty: Vote count across different outcomes and designs; not a response rate or treatment-effect magnitude.
outcomes.primaryStatus: Review outcome; no participant-randomized trial conducted by this publication.

outcomes.name: Adherence/dropout
outcomes.primaryStatus: Review outcome; no participant-randomized trial conducted by this publication.

finding: Eight of 15 trials favored an emotional-skills programme on at least one selected outcome, but only one of five trials using official IPV recidivism records favored the intervention. A count of positive trials does not establish a pooled effect.
limitation: No review registration or published protocol. Heterogeneous interventions and active controls often shared emotional components; four pilot/feasibility trials and frequent self-report limit causal attribution to emotional skills alone.

quality.riskOfBias: Cochrane-domain assessments were conducted independently by two reviewers. No included trial met all domains; ten had insufficient outcome-assessor masking information, and eleven had medium/high other-bias concerns.
quality.attrition: Thirteen trials reported dropout or dose; three had low adherence under the review definition. No significant advantage in dropout or dose was established.
quality.confounding: No review registration or published protocol. Heterogeneous interventions and active controls often shared emotional components; four pilot/feasibility trials and frequent self-report limit causal attribution to emotional skills alone.

quality.transferLimits: No review registration or published protocol. Heterogeneous interventions and active controls often shared emotional components; four pilot/feasibility trials and frequent self-report limit causal attribution to emotional skills alone.

title: The Effectiveness of Culturally Specific Male Domestic Violence Offender Intervention Programs on Behavior Changes and Mental Health: A Systematic Review.
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
interventionFamily: Culturally specific perpetrator programmes using appropriate languages, culturally knowledgeable facilitators, discussion of gender norms and sometimes traditional healing.

relevance.exposureEvidence: Eligibility and study population descriptions explicitly concern IPV perpetrators, IPV-exposed survivors/children, or IPV prevention.
relevance.rationale: Adds culturally relevant intervention context while preserving the negative controlled finding and limits of largely uncontrolled evidence.
relevance.transferLimit: Small and culturally restricted evidence base, inconsistent outcomes and heavy reliance on perpetrator reports. The review text also contains a cross-reference mismatch when attributing one study’s success rate; no exact success percentage is carried forward.

age.reportedRange: Not established from the inspected source sections.

outcomes.result: Mostly reported improvement in uncontrolled or mixed-methods studies; one controlled comparison was unfavorable

title: The promotion of well-being among children exposed to intimate partner violence: A systematic review of interventions.
interventionFamily: Psychosocial interventions including parenting support, child-parent psychotherapy, CBT and case management directed at children, nonoffending parents or families.

relevance.population: Children and adolescents exposed to IPV, including direct or indirect exposure; child-level outcomes required
